StringWithMarkup.String: Sethoxydim (NP-55) (CAS RN 74051-80-2) was evaluated for toxicity when administered to BD (C57BL/6 x DBA) mice (70/sex/group; control group had 100/sex) in the diet at dose levels of 0, 40, 120, 360, and 1080 ppm. At week 52 of a 104-week study, there were no clinical signs of toxicity reported. A total of 10 mortalities, cause unrelated to treatment, was noted for all groups (1-2 per group), including 1 control male. Mean body weight change for males and females in the 1080 ppm group was significantly different (decreased) from controls, and food consumption was increased. Water consumption for all groups was not affected by treatment. Hematological parameters showed no dose-related effects for all groups, but analysis of blood chemistry revealed decreased glucose levels in males receiving 1080 ppm, decreased A/G ratio in males from the 360 and 1080 ppm groups, and females receiving 40 and 120 ppm NP-55 showed an increased ALP. Necropsy at interim sacrifice (52 weeks) revealed greater absolute and relative (to body weight) liver and spleen weights in males from the 1080 ppm group as compared to controls and females in the 360 and 1080 ppm groups showed a significantly greater liver/body weight ratio. Microscopic examination revealed swollen cells and fatty degeneration in the livers of the 360 and 1080 ppm groups. The interim NOAEL under the conditions of this study was considered to be 120 ppm.

StringWithMarkup.String: Sethoxydim (NP-55) (CAS RN 74051-80-2) was evaluated for developmental toxicity in SPF Sprague-Dawley rats. Groups of 24 pregnant females were administered 2 ml of 40, 100, or 250 mg/kg body weight/day of NP-55 suspended in a 1% sodium carboxymethyl cellulose aqueous solution with 0.1% Tween 80 by oral gavage. Two control groups, vehicle and positive controls, were given an equivalent volume of vehicle only or 200 mg/kg of acetylsalicylic acid (aspirin) suspended in the vehicle. Dosing took place on days 7-17 of gestation, with terminal sacrifice on day 21. No mortalities or clinical signs of maternal toxicity were reported for any group. Significant decreases in body weight gain were noted in dams receiving 100 and 250 mg/kg of NP-55 but there was no difference in net weight gain at sacrifice when compared with controls. The mean absolute weight of the adrenal glands was significantly reduced in females receiving 100 mg/kg NP-55, while the 250 mg/kg group showed increased mean absolute and relative liver weights and decreased mean and absolute adrenal weights. No significant changes were reported for spleen, kidney, or ovary mean and absolute weights in any groups receiving NP-55. Females treated with aspirin showed decreased body weight gain on days 16-19, but net body weight gain was reported as being increased at terminal sacrifice when compared to controls. Mean absolute and relative liver and spleen weights were increased, while those of the adrenal glands were significantly decreased in females treated with 200 mg/kg aspirin. Mean implantation sites, corpora lutea, sex ratio, and litter size were not affected by treatment at any dose level. There was a low, non-dose related incidence (0.3%-0.7%) of external variations in all NP-55 treated groups, however, fetuses from the aspirin group showed significantly higher incidence of craniorachischisis (5.1%) over controls and NP-55 treated groups. A slight increase over controls in the incidence of a 14th rudimentary rib in fetuses from the 250 mg/kg group was reported, but there was no evidence of a dose relationship.

StringWithMarkup.String: Sethoxydim's production may result in its release to the environment through various waste streams; it's use as a herbicide will result in its direct release to the environment. If released to air, a vapor pressure of 1.6X10-7 mm Hg at 20-25 °C indicates sethoxydim will exist in both the vapor and particulate phases atmosphere. Vapor-phase sethoxydim will be degraded in the atmosphere by reaction with photochemically-produced hydroxyl radicals; the half-life for this reaction in air is estimated to be 1 day. Particulate-phase sethoxydim will be removed from the atmosphere by wet and dry deposition. Sethoxydim has been shown to be stable to light. If released to soil, sethoxydim is expected to have moderate mobility based upon an estimated Koc of 190; however, very little leaching of sethoxydim into soil has been reported. Based on a reported half-lives of 4 weeks in clay and 2 weeks in sandy loam, biodegradation may be an important environmental fate process in soil. Volatilization from water and moist soil surfaces is not expected to be an important fate process based upon an estimated Henry's Law constant of 2.2X10-11 atm-cu m/mole. Sethoxydim will not volatilize from dry soil surfaces based upon its vapor pressure. If released into water, sethoxydim is expected to adsorb to suspended solids and sediment based upon the estimated Koc. An estimated BCF of 11 suggests the potential for bioconcentration in aquatic organisms is low. Sethoxydim has reported hydrolysis half-lives in water of 1.6, 45, and 438 days at pH 3, 6, and 9, respectively. Occupational exposure to sethoxydim may occur through dermal contact with this compound at workplaces where sethoxydim is produced or used.  (SRC)

Section.Description: Sorption to soils and sediments is an important factor on the transport and fate of organic contaminants in the environment.  The soil/water adsorption coefficient, also known as solid-water distribution coefficient (Kd), measures the amount of chemical substance adsorbed onto soil per amount of water.  Since adsorption occurs predominantly by partition into the soil organic matter, it is more useful to normalize the Kd value to the organic carbon content of a soil and express the distribution coefficient in Koc (organic carbon normalized distribution coefficient).  The greater the Kd (or Koc) value, the less likely a chemical will leach or contribute to runoff.  A very high value means it is strongly adsorbed onto soil and organic matter and does not move throughout the soil.
